original_question: Is there an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes of uniformly bounded degree for which both the 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional coboundary Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients are uniformly bounded below by a positive constant? That is, can one build bounded-degree complexes Xm such that h_0^B(Xm, Sym) and h_1^B(Xm, Sym) are each at least some fixed λ > 0 for all m?
target_in_paper: Section 6.2, Problem 6.5 ("Bounded coboundary expanders in permutations").
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly asks for an infinite family of connected finite polygonal complexes of uniformly bounded degree and a uniform constant λ > 0 such that both h_0^B(X_m, Sym) and h_1^B(X_m, Sym) are bounded below by λ for every m. That is exactly the official open problem stated in Section 6.2 as Problem 6.5, rather than the neighboring Problem 6.6.
missing_details: The exact target is an open problem in Section 6.2, labeled Problem 6.5; it should be identified as such rather than phrased as a broad informal question.
The family is explicitly {X_m}_{m=1}^∞ of connected finite polygonal complexes; here a polygonal complex means a 2-dimensional CW complex whose 2-cells are attached along cyclically reduced paths.
The paper defines "uniformly bounded" precisely: there exists a single integer k > 0 such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k.
The quantifier is "for every m ∈ N," not merely "for all sufficiently large m."
The coefficient object is not a field or ring: it is Sym = ⨆_{n≥2} Sym(n), the disjoint union of symmetric groups, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance with errors d_h.

The Cheeger constants depend on the standing choice of probability distributions μ_i on oriented i-cells; these measures are assumed throughout Section 2 and the resulting distances and norms are μ_i-weighted.
In the non-abelian permutation-coefficient setting, the relevant cocycle/coboundary theory is only defined in dimensions i = 0 and i = 1.

To make the question fully stand-alone, h_i^B(X, Sym) should be identified as h_i^B(X, Sym) = inf { ||δα|| / d(α, B_i(X, Sym)) : α ∈ C^i(X, Sym) \ B_i(X, Sym) }, with d and ||·|| coming from the weighted Hamming metric setup of Section 2.
Problem 6.6 is a different nearby problem, asking for lower bounds on h_0, h_1, and CoSyst_1; it is presented only as a potentially easier task and should not replace Problem 6.5.
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite family {X_m}_{m=1}^∞ of connected finite polygonal complexes (that is, finite 2-dimensional CW complexes with polygonal 2-cells attached along cyclically reduced loops), each equipped with the probability distributions on oriented cells assumed in Section 2, and a constant k ∈ N such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k, together with a constant λ > 0, for which one has h_i^B(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ for every m ∈ N and for i = 0, 1? Here Sym means ⨆_{n≥2} Sym(n) with the normalized Hamming distance with errors d_h, and h_i^B(X, Sym) is the coboundary Cheeger constant h_i^B(X, Sym) = inf { ||δα|| / d(α, B_i(X, Sym)) : α ∈ C^i(X, Sym) \ B_i(X, Sym) }.
justification: The draft is targeting the exact official statement of Problem 6.5 in Section 6.2, since it asks for a bounded-degree infinite family with simultaneous uniform lower bounds on the 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional coboundary Cheeger constants with permutation coefficients. I did not replace it by Problem 6.6, because the paper explicitly presents Problem 6.6 only as a "potentially easier task," not as the same problem. The main hidden assumptions needed to make the question fully stand-alone come from Section 2: polygonal complexes are 2-dimensional CW complexes of the specified type; the metrics and norms depend on probability measures on oriented cells; the coefficient system is the metric group Sym with normalized Hamming distance; and in the non-abelian permutation setup the relevant theory is only defined for i = 0, 1.
